narration: Most people think Medicare in retirement is basically free. But the IRS built a hidden trap that can cost you $3,400 more every single year — and almost nobody warns you it exists.
visual: Medicare card SVG animates in, large red warning triangle pulses above it, '$3,400' drops down in accent red. Dark background.

narration: It's called IRMAA. If your income tops $103,000 as a single retiree, Medicare charges you a surcharge on top of your normal premium. Just one dollar over and the penalty kicks in immediately.
visual: Light background. Animated income bar chart — blue bar grows upward, crosses a dashed red line labeled '$103K THRESHOLD,' bar flashes red. Warning icon appears above the line.

narration: And here's the wild part — you can trigger it by accident. Selling your home, taking a Required Minimum Distribution, or doing a Roth conversion can each push you right over that line without any warning.
visual: Dark background. Three icons spring in one by one: a house with a dollar sign, a jar labeled 'IRA' with an arrow, and a box labeled 'IRA' converting to 'ROTH' with a warning triangle.

narration: Number one, the surcharge hits Medicare Part B. Number two, it hits Part D too. Combined, you could owe over three thousand four hundred dollars more — every single year.
visual: Light background. Two horizontal bars animate in labeled 'MEDICARE PART B' ($2,800/yr) and 'MEDICARE PART D' ($612/yr). A red box animates in showing 'TOTAL EXTRA COST: $3,412/yr'.

narration: What's brutal is the IRS charges you based on income from two years ago. So a Roth conversion you do today could hit your Medicare bill in 2026 — and by then, there's nothing you can do.
visual: Dark background. Two calendar icons: '2024' in blue with 'Roth conversion' text, an arrow labeled '2 YEARS,' and '2026' in red with '$3,400 surcharge hits you NOW.' Red text below: 'By then, it's too late.'

narration: The fix is simple — plan your retirement income to stay just under that threshold. One conversation with a CPA before you convert could save you thousands. Follow for more money traps like this.
visual: Dark background. Three icons spring in: a suited person (CPA), a calculator showing '$103K,' and a pink piggy bank with a coin. A pulsing red CTA button: 'FOLLOW FOR MORE MONEY TRAPS LIKE THIS.'
